verification_notes: Knee OA 5-class Kellgren-Lawrence (KL 0-4) severity grading on the OAI Kaggle dataset (9,786 knee radiographs; 80:20 train/test split). | G1, G2: Compares a custom 3-convolutional-layer CNN trained from scratch (CCNN) against fine-tuned ImageNet VGG16 (FVGG, top layers unfrozen) and a validation-weighted softmax probability ensemble (EA, Eq. 5, §3.4 p. 4-5). Uses offline geometric/photometric data augmentation as an oversampling technique to balance class distributions across KL 0-4 (Abstract p. 1, §3.5 p. 5). | Tables 2 and 3 (pp. 5-6) provide a controlled comparison of CCNN vs. FVGG vs. EA and 'Before Augmentation' vs. 'After Augmentation' (oversampling) across 50-250 epochs: at 250 epochs, FVGG improves from 90.0% to 96.8% and EA from 91.5% to 98.0%, whereas CCNN drops from 73.09% to 58.8%. Methodological concern: Image-level 80:20 split (Q3_patient=N) and likely pre-split augmentation/oversampling leakage explain the implausibly high 98.0% 5-class KL accuracy on OAI.

method: EfficientNet-B3 and ConvNeXt-Tiny, focal loss, class-aware augmentation; class-weighted vs standard sampling; TTA; weighted probability ensemble
key_comparison: Sampling & TTA comparison on 4-class test set (n=1,656, all with Focal Loss gamma=2): (1) 15% EfficientNet-B3 + 85% ConvNeXt-Tiny Ensemble + TTA (Table VI, p. 197): Standard (unweighted) sampling achieved Acc 82.50%, Macro-Rec 79.92%, Macro-Pre 82.64%, Macro-Spec 92.26%, Macro-F1 81.06%, MCC 0.6997, Kappa 0.6980 (QWK ~0.857, p. 196), MR 17.51%; Class-weighted sampling (WeightedRandomSampler) improved all metrics to Acc 83.00% (+0.50%), Macro-Rec 81.26% (+1.34%), Macro-Pre 82.81%, Macro-Spec 93.05%, Macro-F1 81.94% (+0.88%), MCC 0.7141 (+0.0144), Kappa 0.7135 (+0.0155), MR 17.03% (and G2 sensitivity rose from 63.31% to 75.8%, Fig. 2b; G2 PR-AUC rose from 0.76 to 0.79, Fig. 4). (2) Single models & TTA across sampling regimes (Fig. 8, p. 201): Under Standard sampling (No-TTA -> TTA): EfficientNet-B3 77.8% -> 79.2%, ConvNeXt-Tiny 82.9% -> 83.1%, 15/85 Ensemble 81.4% -> 82.5%. Under Class-weighted sampling (No-TTA -> TTA): EfficientNet-B3 78.4% -> 79.6%, ConvNeXt-Tiny 82.6% -> 83.8% (best overall), 15/85 Ensemble 82.0% -> 83.0% (55/45 Ensemble: 82.07%, Macro-F1 80.66%). (3) Bootstrap 95% CIs (N=1,000, Fig. 7, pp. 199-200): Standard TTA: EfficientNet-B3 79.2% [77.2-81.2%], ConvNeXt-Tiny 83.1% [81.3-84.9%], Ensemble 82.5% [80.6-84.4%]; Class-weighted TTA: EfficientNet-B3 80.37% [78.50-82.19%], ConvNeXt-Tiny 82.85% [81.10-84.66%], Ensemble 82.92% [81.22-84.72%] (overlapping CIs confirm ensemble is not statistically superior to ConvNeXt-Tiny alone).
